entity_types.name: ChipVendor
entity_types.description: Merchant data-center AI accelerator (GPU) vendor selling silicon on the open market; the supply-side price-setter whose revenue share is the central question.

attributes.name: role
attributes.description: Market role (e.g. dominant incumbent vs. merchant challenger vs. trailing vendor)

attributes.name: stance
attributes.description: Strategic posture toward defending or attacking accelerator share

attributes.name: market_share
attributes.description: Estimated merchant data-center accelerator revenue share (%)

attributes.name: product_roadmap
attributes.description: Core GPU roadmap (e.g. Blackwell->Rubin, MI300->MI400/Helios, Gaudi)

entity_types.name: Foundry
entity_types.description: Leading-edge contract chip manufacturer and advanced-packaging (CoWoS) supplier that gatekeeps who can physically ship AI silicon.

attributes.name: role
attributes.description: Foundry positioning (dominant leader vs. second-source aspirant vs. IDM/foundry challenger)

attributes.name: process_node
attributes.description: Leading-edge node capability (e.g. N3/N2/A16, SF3/SF2 GAA, 18A/14A)

attributes.name: influence_tier
attributes.description: Bottleneck/allocation power over the accelerator supply chain (high|medium|low)

entity_types.name: MemoryMaker
entity_types.description: HBM (high-bandwidth memory) supplier whose constrained, oligopoly-priced capacity is a binding input to every AI accelerator.

attributes.name: role
attributes.description: HBM positioning (leader vs. qualified second/third source)

attributes.name: market_share
attributes.description: Estimated HBM market share / supply rank

attributes.name: motivation
attributes.description: Core driver (e.g. lock multiyear NVIDIA allocation, close HBM4 gap)

entity_types.name: EquipmentMaker
entity_types.description: Semiconductor capital-equipment supplier (notably EUV lithography) on the critical path of leading-edge AI-chip manufacturing.

attributes.name: role
attributes.description: Equipment role (e.g. monopoly EUV/High-NA lithography supplier)

attributes.name: influence_tier
attributes.description: Criticality to the AI supply chain (high|medium|low)

attributes.name: motivation
attributes.description: Core driver (e.g. ramp High-NA EUV, manage China export exposure)

entity_types.name: Hyperscaler
entity_types.description: Cloud/platform giant that both buys merchant GPUs at scale and builds captive custom AI ASICs to cut cost-per-token and supply risk.

attributes.name: role
attributes.description: Dual role as largest GPU buyer and custom-ASIC builder

attributes.name: stance
attributes.description: Posture toward shifting workloads from merchant GPUs to in-house silicon

attributes.name: custom_silicon
attributes.description: In-house accelerator program (TPU/Trainium/Maia/MTIA)

entity_types.name: CustomSiliconPartner
entity_types.description: Merchant ASIC and AI-networking supplier that co-designs hyperscaler custom accelerators (XPUs), monetizing the GPU-to-ASIC shift as the arms dealer.

attributes.name: role
attributes.description: Custom-silicon role (lead XPU co-designer vs. secondary challenger)

attributes.name: stance
attributes.description: Posture as the primary beneficiary of the captive-ASIC shift

attributes.name: motivation
attributes.description: Core driver (e.g. grow XPU customers, win sockets vs. rival)

entity_types.name: AILab
entity_types.description: Frontier AI model lab whose enormous training/inference compute appetite drives accelerator demand and supplier diversification.

attributes.name: role
attributes.description: Demand-side role (largest compute driver, custom-silicon aspirant, multi-silicon adopter)

attributes.name: stance
attributes.description: Silicon strategy (single-supplier vs. multi-silicon vs. own-chip ambitions)

attributes.name: motivation
attributes.description: Core driver (secure maximal compute, cut cost-per-token, escape GPU scarcity)

entity_types.name: Neocloud
entity_types.description: Specialized GPU cloud or capacity reseller that buys and leases large NVIDIA accelerator fleets to AI labs and hyperscalers.

attributes.name: role
attributes.description: Capacity-reseller role (pure-play neocloud vs. OCI-style hyperscaler reseller)

attributes.name: influence_tier
attributes.description: Weight in accelerator demand and allocation (high|medium|low)

attributes.name: vulnerability
attributes.description: Key fragility (leverage/GPU-collateral, single-vendor/customer concentration)

entity_types.name: SiliconChallenger
entity_types.description: Domestic-substitution or niche AI-silicon vendor offering an alternative architecture to merchant GPUs (China substitute or wafer-scale/LPU startup).

attributes.name: role

attributes.name: stance

attributes.name: market_share

entity_types.name: Regulator

analysis_summary: This ontology models the data-center AI accelerator market through end-2027, centered on whether NVIDIA retains >=75% merchant accelerator revenue share against hyperscaler custom ASICs and AMD Instinct. Ten entity types capture the full value chain by behavioral role: ChipVendor (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel) is the supply-side share contender; Foundry (TSMC, Samsung Foundry, Intel Foundry) gatekeeps via leading-edge nodes and CoWoS allocation; MemoryMaker (SK Hynix, Samsung, Micron) supplies bottlenecked HBM; EquipmentMaker (ASML) holds the EUV monopoly upstream; Hyperscaler (Google, AWS, Microsoft, Meta) simultaneously buys GPUs and builds captive ASICs (TPU/Trainium/Maia/MTIA); CustomSiliconPartner (Broadcom, Marvell) co-designs those XPUs as the arms dealer of the ASIC shift; AILab (OpenAI, Anthropic) drives frontier compute demand and supplier diversification; Neocloud (CoreWeave, Oracle, xAI) resells NVIDIA capacity at leveraged scale; SiliconChallenger (Huawei, Cerebras, Groq, SambaNova) offers China-substitution or niche architectures; and Regulator (BIS, China MIIT) reshapes demand geography via export controls and self-sufficiency policy. Person (Jensen Huang, Lisa Su) and Organization (SemiAnalysis, TrendForce, Morgan Stanley, Arm) serve as fallback types. Ten edge types encode the researched taxonomy (COMPETES_WITH, DEPENDS_ON, PARTNERS_WITH, REGULATES, OPPOSES, ALLY_OF, INFLUENCES) plus domain-specific supply-chain edges (SUPPLIES, CO_DESIGNS, FABRICATES_FOR), each carrying sentiment, strength, since_date, and a grounded basis. Together these support simulating the decisive share dynamics: the denominator definition (merchant vs. captive ASICs at transfer value), training-vs-inference segmentation, CUDA lock-in vs. open stacks, CoWoS/HBM4 allocation races, and US-China decoupling driving Huawei/SMIC substitution.
